title: Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory: the two-leg scalar bound (Theorem 3.1)
author: Benoît Collins and Wangjun Yuan
work: Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's main two-leg scalar operator-norm bound, printed as Theorem 3.1 (source0.tex lines 706-714), delivered with the paper's own complete proof (lines 1474-1481). The counted proof is the paper's final assembly and is short on purpose: it takes the lower bound from the retained Theorem 5.1, which is attained by a tuple of permuting tensors built from the matrix U = sum E_ij (x) E_ji, and the upper bound from the retained Theorem 4.1, which pairs a full simple partial graph with its complement by Cauchy-Schwarz and evaluates both Hilbert-Schmidt norms as powers of N. What makes the unit research-level is the retained chain that the assembly closes over, and that chain is delivered in full: the graphical calculus in which a partial trace becomes a graph of rectangles joined by coloured directed edges, the theory of simple and full partial graphs with the cycle-cut parameters M and C, the contraction identity, the Hilbert-Schmidt norm Lemma 4.4 with its 297-line induction over the graph cases, and the permutation-tensor evaluation of the lower bound. No qualifying examination poses an operator-norm bound for multi-leg matrix tensors obtained by balancing a graph against its complement; the ingredients are paper-specific and the assembly is the paper's own, so the unit is H2 rather than H3.
